fix: keep valid GPS longitudes in the EXIF GPS migration

MigrateForExifGPSCorrection runs on every startup and clears GPS data whenever |longitude| > 90. Longitude ranges over [-180, 180], so this deletes valid coordinates for everything east of 90°E or west of 90°W.

The EXIF scanner itself has already been fixed in #1260.

Changes:
1. Only clear longitudes beyond ±180 in the migration.
2. The corresponding test now checks that the valid data is kept.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected GPS coordinate validation to accept longitudes within the valid ±180° range. Previously, valid coordinates with longitude values beyond ±90° could be removed.
  * Latitude values beyond ±90° and longitude values beyond ±180° continue to be treated as invalid, with both coordinates cleared when either value is out of range.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

fix(forge): a merged release pull request is recognised again

## What

- `toPullRequest` reads a merge from `pr.GetMerged() || !pr.GetMergedAt().IsZero()`, so a pull
  request that came from the list endpoint is recognised as merged.
- A comment names the go-github fields the list operation does not populate, so the next reader
  does not fall into the same hole.
- Tests: `TestToPullRequest` pins the mapping without the network, `TestPullRequests` uses a list
  fixture of the real shape, no `merged` key and a `merged_at` on the merged entry, and
  `TestPullRequestsListedMergeTimestampDrivesRelease` drives a merged pull request from a list
  response through `release.Run` against an httptest server.

## Why

- Merging release pull request #19, `chore(main): release v0.1.0-rc.1`, produced no tag, no
  GitHub release and no label swap. The run printed `created chore(main): release v0.1.0` and
  `nothing to release`.
- `release.Run` lists closed pull requests on the release branch and skips everything that is not
  `Merged`. `Merged` came from go-github's `merged` field, which GitHub returns only from the
  single pull request endpoint, so every listed pull request read as not merged and nothing was
  ever released.
- The fake forge sets `Merged` directly, so every test passed on a value the real forge could not
  produce.

## Verification

- `task check` green: golangci-lint, vet, markdownlint, yamllint, actionlint, goreleaser check,
  hadolint, shellcheck, gitleaks, `go test -race`, action shell tests, build.
- Each new test was run against the unfixed mapping: the mapping case reads `Merged: false`, and
  `release.Run` returns an empty slice, which is exactly the reported symptom.
- Checked the rest of the mapping against go-github's "not populated by the List operation"
  comment: `Number`, `Title`, `Body`, `Labels`, `URL` and `HeadSHA` are all carried by the list
  endpoint. `MergeCommitSHA` is not part of `forge.PullRequest`; `internal/release` reads the
  merge commit through `Forge.MergeCommit`, which always calls the single pull request endpoint.

## Risk

- The next run on the default branch releases what this bug swallowed: `v0.1.0-rc.1` from #19's
  merge commit `d6da3783237c293cd636284c5a8c8c043e8a1927`, with the label swap to
  `release: tagged`. That is the intended recovery.
- The open release pull request #37, `chore(main): release v0.1.0`, is unaffected and releases
  the stable version when it merges.
- `forgetest.Fake` is unchanged: `Merged` is a field of the normalised interface type, which the
  fixed forge produces from either endpoint.

Closes #38

fix(cask): keep generated casks loadable on Intel

> 🤖 Generated by the Agentic Engineer

<!--
Write for the project manager deciding whether this change is needed — not for
a code reviewer (CodeRabbit and CI validate correctness). Keep it SHORT:
1–3 plain-language sentences per section. No code detail — no file paths,
symbols, snippets, or test/lint output. The change type lives in the PR title
(Conventional Commits), not here.
-->

## Why

Homebrew rejects both generated casks on Intel because the older fallback overlaps the metadata now supplied by the release tool. This blocks the normal release handoff.

## What

Use the release tool’s checksum and architecture restriction, and check both generated casks across every supported host variant before accepting release configuration changes. Regeneration and public release verification remain on the linked issue.

Part of #7943

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Exercise the real GoReleaser -> brew style -> all-platform cask loader boundary (#7943).
+# Only the build payload is replaced with a tiny fixture; cask configuration comes from this repo.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+for tool in go goreleaser yq brew jq git; do
+	command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || {
+		printf 'missing required tool: %s\n' "$tool" >&2
+		exit 1
+	}
+done
+
+export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1
+work="$(mktemp -d)"
+# Homebrew 7 requires trust before readall will inspect a non-official tap. Isolate this test's
+# trust store so a skipped, untrusted tap cannot report success or alter the user's trust list.
+export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$work/config"
+tap="agentic-validation/cask-render-$$-${RANDOM}"
+tap_added=false
+completed=false
+# cleanup retires the temporary tap and fixtures while preserving any failure status.
+cleanup() {
+	result=$?
+	if ! "$completed" && [[ "$result" -eq 0 ]]; then result=1; fi
+	if "$tap_added"; then
+		brew untap --force "$tap" || result=1
+	fi
+	rm -rf "$work"
+	exit "$result"
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+mkdir -p "$work/tap/Casks"
+for name in ksail ksail-desktop; do
+	config=.goreleaser.yaml
+	if [[ "$name" == ksail-desktop ]]; then config=.goreleaser.desktop.yaml; fi
+	fixture="$work/$name"
+	mkdir -p "$fixture"
+	printf 'module cask-render-fixture\n\ngo 1.27.3\n' >"$fixture/go.mod"
+	printf 'package main\nfunc main() {}\n' >"$fixture/main.go"
+	# Keep the real archive/target/cask shapes. Remove application-only build hooks and publication
+	# credentials, and force upload off; this fixture must never publish or use a credential.
+	yq '.project_name = "'"$name"'" | .dist = "dist" |
+		.before.hooks = [] | .builds[].main = "." | .builds[].tags = [] |
+		.builds[].env = ["CGO_ENABLED=0"] | .builds[].hooks = {} | .builds[].ldflags = [] |
+		.archives[].files = [] | .homebrew_casks[].skip_upload = "true" |
+		.homebrew_casks[].repository.token = "" |
+		del(.homebrew_casks[].commit_author.signing, .dockers_v2, .docker_signs, .release.extra_files)' \
+		"$root/$config" >"$fixture/.goreleaser.yaml"
+	git -C "$fixture" init --quiet
+	git -C "$fixture" remote add origin https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail.git
+	git -C "$fixture" add go.mod main.go .goreleaser.yaml
+	git -C "$fixture" -c user.name=fixture -c user.email=fixture@example.invalid \
+		-c commit.gpgsign=false commit --quiet -m fixture
+	git -C "$fixture" tag v7.204.0
+	(
+		cd "$fixture"
+		goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=validate,publish,announce,sign
+	)
+	casks=()
+	while IFS= read -r file; do casks+=("$file"); done < <(find "$fixture/dist" -name "$name.rb" -type f)
+	[[ ${#casks[@]} -eq 1 ]] || {
+		printf 'expected one generated %s cask\n' "$name" >&2
+		exit 1
+	}
+	brew style --fix "${casks[0]}"
+	cp "${casks[0]}" "$work/tap/Casks/$name.rb"
+done
+
+git -C "$work/tap" init --quiet
+git -C "$work/tap" add Casks/ksail.rb Casks/ksail-desktop.rb
+git -C "$work/tap" -c user.name=fixture -c user.email=fixture@example.invalid \
+	-c commit.gpgsign=false commit --quiet -m fixture
+brew tap --custom-remote "$tap" "$work/tap"
+tap_added=true
+brew trust "$tap"
+brew readall --os=all --arch=all "$tap"
+
+# This runner is macOS. Both casks must retain a real checksum and the architecture
+# requirement after rendering and style cleanup; no product binary is installed or executed.
+for name in ksail ksail-desktop; do
+	brew info --cask --json=v2 "$tap/$name" >"$work/$name.json"
+	jq -e '.casks | length == 1' "$work/$name.json" >/dev/null
+	jq -e '.casks[0].sha256 | test("^[0-9a-f]{64}$")' "$work/$name.json" >/dev/null
+	jq -e '.casks[0].depends_on.arch | any(.type == "arm" and .bits == 64)' "$work/$name.json" >/dev/null
+done
+printf 'PASS: both rendered casks load on every platform and preserve checksum/architecture guards\n'
+completed=true
